title: release v2.2.0
description: P18-P26 signed off and the tree is green, so the work goes out. MINOR rather than patch, decided by the maintainer: two new flags (/audit:status --view and --json --section) are new functionality, and the DEFAULT human render changes - somebody pinning ~2.1.x would get a different output from a command they already run. COMPATIBILITY.md protects meta.version and the config keys the plugin reads, not terminal layout, so no promise is broken either way; the version is what tells a reader which of those two happened. One commit bumps plugin.json, finalizes the CHANGELOG section and carries the annotated tag, and the followers a bump stales are redone in the order tools/verify.sh --release prints: README curl pins, rendered artifacts, docs/index.html as a byte copy of the example report, then screenshots - capture FOLLOWS the bump, never precedes it.
desiredOutcome: v2.2.0 is published: one commit carrying the bump, the finalized CHANGELOG and the annotated tag; every follower redone in order; CI green on that commit before the push; and a GitHub Release created for the tag so the README's fetch pins resolve to a page a reader lands on.

tasks.title: Bump to 2.2.0 and redo every follower the bump stales, in order
tasks.description: plugin.json to 2.2.0; CHANGELOG [Unreleased] becomes [2.2.0] with today's date; the three curl pins in plugins/audit/README.md move from v2.1.1 to v2.2.0 so a reader fetches the files this release ships; the committed rendered artifacts re-render because each stamps the version that produced it, in the page and again in its embedded Markdown twin; docs/index.html is a byte copy so it follows the artifact it copies; screenshots come last because each image records the version it was shot at, and capturing before the bump invalidates every picture. Then tools/verify.sh --release, which asserts the followers rather than repairing them.
